introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Economics 3 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2022. Duration: 1 hour 45 minutes.**

INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES: Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:
> "Speaking to journalist in 1997, at a Press Conference in Douala, GICAM President harped on the need for Economic operators, Opinion Leaders and Pressure Groups to bring pressure to bear on their respective Governments to promote Economic Integration in the Region. He regretted that, contrary to what obtains in other regions, there was no free movement of people and goods in Central Africa. Taking the Livestock sector as an example, he regretted that Cameroonian meat would sell more expensively in Gabon than meat from South Africa situated thousands of kilometers away".

*Source: Adapted from "The Herald No 547 of 1997"*
incertitudes: Question 5(b)(ii) : « the trade blocs mentioned in (a) above » renvoie à la zone de libre-échange et à l'union douanière de la question (a) ; le corrigé retient l'union douanière (tarif extérieur commun), en précisant que la CEMAC est aussi une union monétaire.
Question 5(c) et (e) : les problèmes et avantages de la CEMAC sont donnés sous forme qualitative (aucun chiffre réel) ; le passage date de 1997 et la situation de la CEMAC a évolué depuis.
Le sujet imprime « kilometers » (orthographe américaine) et « Speaking to journalist » (sans article) : conservés tels quels.

Aucun total n'est imprimé par question (« All questions carry equal marks ») : `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide ; les points de chaque sous-question (a), (b)... sont la somme des points imprimés de ses parties ; la somme des points imprimés de chaque question vaut 20.

questions.enonce_markdown: With the aid of examples, distinguish between a free trade area and a customs union. (6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**A free trade area** is a group of countries that **abolish tariffs, quotas and other trade barriers on trade among themselves**, but **each member keeps its own tariffs and trade policy towards non-members**. Because each member sets its own external tariff, goods from a non-member could enter the area through the member with the lowest tariff, so rules of origin are needed. Examples: the European Free Trade Association (EFTA), the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA, now USMCA), the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).

**A customs union** has **all the features of a free trade area** (free trade among members) **plus a common external tariff (CET)** on imports from non-members, and often a common trade policy. Goods from outside pay the same duty whichever member they enter, so there is no need for rules of origin. Examples: the original European Economic Community, CEMAC, the Southern African Customs Union (SACU), the East African Community.

| | Free trade area | Customs union |
|---|---|---|
| Trade among members | Free | Free |
| Tariff against non-members | Each member sets its own | Common external tariff |
| Trade policy | Independent | Common |
| Degree of integration | Lower (first stage) | Higher (second stage) |

A customs union is thus a deeper form of integration than a free trade area; the next stages are a common market (free movement of labour and capital) and an economic and monetary union.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Give the full meaning of "CEMAC". (2 marks)

(ii) To which of the trade blocs mentioned in (a) above does "CEMAC" belong? (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) CEMAC** stands for the **Central African Economic and Monetary Community** (in French, *Communauté Économique et Monétaire de l'Afrique Centrale*). Its six member states are Cameroon, the Central African Republic, Chad, the Republic of Congo, Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.

**(ii)** CEMAC belongs to the **customs union**: its members trade freely with one another and apply a **common external tariff** to imports from outside the community. It is also a **monetary union**, with a common currency, the CFA franc (XAF or FCFA), issued by a common central bank (BEAC).

questions.enonce_markdown: Enumerate any three problems faced by "CEMAC". (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any three problems (1 mark each):

1. **Poor transport and communication links** between member countries (few roads and railways in bad condition), which raise transport costs and hinder trade.
2. **Non-tariff barriers and weak application of the rules of free movement**: many roadblocks and checkpoints, informal payments, slow customs procedures and visa or residence formalities, so goods and people do not move freely, as the passage complains.
3. **Similar economies (low complementarity).** Members export similar primary products (oil, timber, cocoa, coffee, cotton) to the outside world, so trade among themselves is small.
4. **Political instability and insecurity** in some member states, which discourage investment and trade.
5. **Unequal sharing of the benefits and costs of integration**, loss of customs revenue and lack of political will to apply decisions.
6. **Overlapping membership of other groupings** and the dependence of members on markets outside the region.

questions.enonce_markdown: Give two reasons why South African goods may be cheaper than Cameroonian goods in a CEMAC country. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any two reasons (2 marks each, with explanation):

1. **Lower costs of production in South Africa.** South Africa is much more industrialised, and its commercial livestock farms and processors use modern technology and produce on a large scale. They enjoy **economies of scale** and high productivity, so their unit cost is low.
2. **High internal trade costs in CEMAC.** Cameroonian meat has to cross poor roads and many checkpoints, and pays informal levies and non-tariff charges, so its delivered price in Gabon is high, whereas South African meat is shipped in bulk by sea.
3. **Trade policy.** South African goods may enter at low tariffs, or the exporters may receive subsidies and export incentives, so that the price in the importing country is lower. The exchange rate of the South African currency can also make its goods cheap.

This is the point of the passage: in the absence of free movement of goods inside the region, outside suppliers can sell more cheaply than neighbours.

questions.enonce_markdown: List three advantages of Cameroon belonging to "CEMAC". (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Any three advantages (1 mark each):

1. **A larger market.** Cameroonian producers can sell to the whole community without tariffs, which allows production on a larger scale, lower unit costs and the growth of industry.
2. **A common currency.** The common currency removes exchange-rate risk and conversion costs between members and helps to keep prices stable, with low inflation.
3. **Free movement of goods, labour and capital** (in principle), which allows resources to go where they are most productive and widens the choice of consumers.
4. **Common external tariff.** It protects the region's young industries against outside competition.
5. **Greater bargaining power** in negotiations with the rest of the world, and more attraction for foreign investors because of the larger market.
6. **Shared infrastructure and cooperation** in projects such as roads, energy and security.
